entries.head: follow up

senses.zh: 过一段时间再联系推进
senses.en: to contact someone again about something not yet finished

example.en: I'll follow up with the client on Monday.
example.zh: 我周一再跟客户联系。

entries.l1_note: “跟进”不是 follow（跟着走）；商务场景必须 follow up。

entries.head: put forward

senses.en: to suggest an idea for other people to consider

example.en: I put forward a plan for working from home two days a week.
example.zh: 我提了个一周两天远程的方案。

entries.l1_note: “提出”不是 put out（那是熄灭、拿出）；提建议用 put forward。

entries.head: reach out

senses.zh: 给别人发消息或打电话
senses.en: to contact someone to ask for help or offer something

example.en: Feel free to reach out if you have any questions.
example.zh: 有问题随时联系我。

entries.l1_note: 商务邮件里“联系我”不是 contact with me（错），是 reach out to me / contact me。

entries.head: touch base

senses.en: to talk to someone briefly to share updates

example.en: Let's touch base on Friday before the client meeting.
example.zh: 周五见客户前我们先碰一下。

entries.l1_note: 商务口头语，不是“接触基地”；中文没有对应词，别逐字翻。

entries.head: run by
entries.zh: 先给某人过目、征求同意

senses.en: to tell someone an idea to get their opinion

example.en: Let me run this by my manager before we commit.
example.zh: 正式定下来之前我先跟经理过一下这个想法。

entries.l1_note: “跟领导说一下”不是 tell my boss 就完事；run it by someone 是征求同意。代词夹中间。
collocations: run an idea by the team

entries.head: wrap up

senses.en: to finish a meeting or piece of work

example.en: Let's wrap up in five minutes — I have another call.
example.zh: 我们五分钟内收尾吧，我还有个电话会。

entries.l1_note: “收尾”不是 close the meeting 才地道；wrap up 更口语。

entries.head: hand over

senses.en: to give control or responsibility to someone else

example.en: I'll hand over the files before I leave on Friday.
example.zh: 我周五走之前把文件交接好。

collocations: hand over to the new manager
entries.l1_note: 移交是 hand over；hand in 是交作业，别混。

entries.head: take over

senses.zh: 接手别人的工作或职位
senses.en: to take control of a job or company from someone

example.en: She's taking over the account while he's on leave.
example.zh: 他休假期间她接手这个客户。

entries.l1_note: 接手工作不是 take the work over 才自然；take over 后直接跟宾语即可。

entries.head: look into

senses.en: to try to find out the facts about something

example.en: Thanks for the report — I'll look into it today.
example.zh: 谢谢反馈，我今天就去查一下。

entries.l1_note: “调查”不是 look for（那是找东西）；look into 才是查原因。

entries.head: go over
entries.zh: 把内容从头看一遍；走过去；串门

senses.en: to examine or review something carefully

example.en: Let's go over the answers before the test.
example.zh: 考试前我们把答案过一遍。

senses.en: to move towards someone or something

example.en: Go over to the counter and ask for a bag.
example.zh: 去柜台那边要个袋子。

senses.en: to visit someone's home briefly

example.en: We went over to our neighbors' place for tea.
example.zh: 我们去邻居家坐了坐，喝了杯茶。

entries.l1_note: “复习”不是 review it again and again 才自然；go over 更口语。

entries.head: run through
entries.zh: 正式场合前快速演练；贯穿；蔓延

senses.en: to practice or review something quickly

example.en: Let's run through the slides once before we present.
example.zh: 上讲台前我们把幻灯片过一遍。

senses.en: to spread through a place or group

example.en: A wave of excitement ran through the office.
example.zh: 一阵兴奋传遍了办公室。

senses.en: to be present throughout something

example.en: A thread of humor runs through the whole speech.
example.zh: 整篇演讲贯穿着一种幽默。

entries.l1_note: 演练是 run through；run over 是碾过，别混。

entries.head: come up with

senses.en: to think of an idea or solution

example.en: Nobody could come up with a better name for the app.
example.zh: 没人能想出一个更好的 App 名字。

entries.l1_note: “想出”不是 think out / think up（也可以但少）；come up with 后直接跟想出的东西。

entries.head: go ahead

senses.en: used to give someone permission to start

example.en: If you're ready, go ahead and send the email.
example.zh: 准备好了就把邮件发出去吧。

entries.l1_note: “你先来”不是 you first 才地道；go ahead 是许可也是让对方先做。

entries.head: make up
entries.zh: 编造一个说法；吵架后和好；构成

senses.en: to invent an excuse or story

example.en: He made up some excuse about the subway being delayed.
example.zh: 他编了个地铁延误的借口。

senses.en: to become friends again after an argument

example.en: They argued for an hour and made up before dessert.
example.zh: 他们吵了一小时，甜点还没上就和好了。

senses.en: to form or compose something

example.en: Women make up half of the team.
example.zh: 团队里女性占一半。

entries.l1_note: 和好用 make up 或 make up with someone；编故事也是 make up，靠上下文区分。

entries.head: keep up with

senses.en: to stay at the same pace as a discussion or schedule

example.en: I lost the thread after the second slide — I couldn't keep up with the discussion.
example.zh: 第二张幻灯片之后我就跟丢了，跟不上讨论。

entries.l1_note: “跟上”不是 follow up（那是后续跟进）；进度用 keep up with。

entries.head: spell out

senses.en: to explain something in very clear detail

example.en: Let me spell out what the client actually needs.
example.zh: 我把客户到底要什么讲清楚。

entries.l1_note: 讲清楚是 spell out，不是 say clearly（太泛）。

entries.head: lay out

senses.en: to explain something in an organized way

example.en: She laid out three options for the launch.
example.zh: 她把上线的三个方案摆出来讲。

entries.l1_note: lay out 是摊开讲；layout 名词是布局。

entries.head: touch on

senses.en: to mention a subject briefly

example.en: He touched on the budget but didn't give numbers.
example.zh: 他提到了预算但没给数字。

entries.l1_note: 简单提到是 touch on，不是 touch（摸）。

entries.head: sum up

senses.en: to give the main points again

example.en: Let me sum up before we vote.
example.zh: 投票前我先总结一下。

entries.l1_note: 总结是 sum up；不是 summarize up（重复）。

entries.head: follow through

senses.en: to complete what you promised

example.en: He never follows through on anything he says.
example.zh: 他说的话从来没有落实过。

entries.l1_note: 落实是 follow through (on)；follow up 是跟进联系。

entries.head: carry out

senses.en: to do a plan or task

example.en: We carried out the survey over two weeks.
example.zh: 我们用两周完成了这项调查。

entries.l1_note: 执行是 carry out；carry on 是继续。

entries.head: loop in

senses.en: to include someone in a conversation

example.en: Loop in legal before you reply to the client.
example.zh: 回复客户前把法务拉进来。

entries.l1_note: 拉进沟通是 loop in；不是 add to the email（太具体）。

entries.head: call back

senses.en: to phone someone again

example.en: I'll call you back after this meeting.
example.zh: 开完这个会我给你回电话。

entries.l1_note: 回电是 call back；不是 return a call（也行但正式）。

entries.head: hear back

senses.en: to receive a reply from someone

example.en: I applied last week and still haven't heard back.
example.zh: 我上周投的，到现在没回音。

entries.l1_note: 收到回复是 hear back (from)，不是 receive back（中式）。

entries.head: check with

senses.en: to ask someone before deciding

example.en: Check with your manager before you promise a date.
example.zh: 答应日期前先问下经理。

entries.l1_note: 问一下是 check with；check 单独是检查。

entries.head: run past

senses.en: to show an idea to someone for approval

example.en: Run it past the design lead before you build it.
example.zh: 做之前先给设计负责人过一下。

entries.l1_note: 过目征求意见是 run it past someone；代词夹中间。

entries.head: sign off

senses.en: to give official approval

example.en: Finance has to sign off on anything over 10,000.
example.zh: 超过一万的都要财务批。

entries.l1_note: 批准是 sign off (on)；签字≠签名（sign）。

entries.head: iron out

senses.en: to solve small problems

example.en: We ironed out the last few issues before launch.
example.zh: 上线前我们摆平了最后几个问题。

entries.l1_note: 摆平细节是 iron out，画面是熨平。

entries.head: hammer out

senses.en: to reach an agreement after a lot of discussion

example.en: They hammered out a deal after midnight.
example.zh: 过了午夜他们才谈成协议。

entries.l1_note: 谈定是 hammer out，带“反复敲”的意味。

entries.head: pass on

senses.en: to give a message to someone else

example.en: Could you pass on the message to the night shift?
example.zh: 能把这个消息带给夜班吗？

entries.l1_note: 转达是 pass on；pass 是递过去。

entries.head: leave out

senses.en: to not include someone or something

example.en: You left out the client's name in the email.
example.zh: 邮件里你把客户名字漏了。

senses.en: to not consider something

example.en: Don't leave out the delivery fee when you compare prices.
example.zh: 比价的时候别忽略配送费。

entries.l1_note: leave out 是美式“漏掉”；代词夹中间：leave it out。

entries.head: make out

senses.en: to manage to see or hear something

example.en: I can't make out the address on this package.
example.zh: 这个包裹上的地址我看不清。

senses.en: to understand someone or something

example.en: I can't make out what he's trying to say.
example.zh: 我搞不懂他到底想说什么。

entries.l1_note: make out 是“辨认/理解”；make up 是“编造/和好”，别混。

entries.head: come back to

senses.en: to return to a subject in a conversation

example.en: Let's come back to the budget after lunch.
example.zh: 预算的事午饭后再说。

senses.en: to reply to someone later

example.en: I'll come back to you with the numbers tomorrow.
example.zh: 数字我明天回复你。

entries.l1_note: 回到话题用 come back to something；回复某人用 come back to someone。

entries.head: get across to

senses.en: to make someone understand something

example.en: I couldn't get across to him why the deadline moved.
example.zh: 我没法让他明白截止日期为什么改了。

entries.l1_note: get something across to someone；宾语放 across 前面。

entries.head: keep from

senses.en: to prevent someone from doing something

example.en: The rain kept us from going out.
example.zh: 下雨让我们没能出门。

senses.en: to not tell someone something

example.en: She kept the news from her parents for a week.
example.zh: 她把消息瞒了父母一个星期。

entries.l1_note: 阻止义用 keep someone from doing；瞒着义用 keep something from someone。

entries.head: agree with

senses.en: to have the same opinion as someone

example.en: I agree with you about the new schedule.
example.zh: 新排期我同意你的看法。

entries.l1_note: agree with + 人/观点；agree to + 提议/安排；agree on + 共同决定的事。

entries.head: disagree with

senses.en: to have a different opinion

example.en: Several people disagreed with the plan in the meeting.
example.zh: 会上有几个人不同意这个方案。

entries.l1_note: disagree with 是不同意某人/某观点；disagree about 是就某事有分歧。

entries.head: object to

senses.en: to say that you disagree with something

example.en: I object to paying for a seat I didn't choose.
example.zh: 我反对为没选的座位付钱。

entries.l1_note: object to 的 to 是介词，后面跟名词或 doing，不是 do。

entries.head: be opposed to

senses.en: to disagree with and try to stop something

example.en: The neighbors are opposed to the new parking lot.
example.zh: 邻居们反对新建停车场。

entries.l1_note: be opposed to + 名词/doing；比 object to 更正式。

entries.head: refer to

senses.en: to mention someone or something

example.en: The report refers to last year's sales figures.
example.zh: 报告提到了去年的销售数据。

senses.en: to look at something for information

example.en: Refer to the manual before you reset the router.
example.zh: 重置路由器前先看一下说明书。

entries.l1_note: refer to 有两个常用义：提到、查阅；别写成 refer about。

entries.head: relate to

senses.en: to understand how someone feels

example.en: I can relate to what you said about overtime.
example.zh: 你说的加班的事我能理解。

entries.l1_note: relate to 是“理解/与…有关”；be related to 是“与…有亲属/关联”。

entries.head: listen to

senses.en: to give attention to a sound or person

example.en: Listen to the announcement before you board.
example.zh: 登机前听一下广播。

entries.l1_note: listen to + 宾语；listen 单独用是“听”，不能说 listen the music。

entries.head: talk to

senses.en: to have a conversation with someone

example.en: I need to talk to my manager about the shift change.
example.zh: 我得跟经理谈换班的事。

entries.l1_note: talk to 和 talk with 都可以；talk about 是谈某事。
collocations: talk to someone about a problem

entries.head: talk with

senses.en: to have a conversation with someone

example.en: She talked with the client for half an hour.
example.zh: 她和客户谈了半小时。

entries.l1_note: talk with 更强调双向交流；美式常用。

entries.head: ask about

senses.en: to ask for information about something

example.en: He asked about the delivery time.
example.zh: 他问了送达时间。

entries.l1_note: ask about 是问某事；ask for 是索要。

entries.head: know about

senses.en: to have information about something

example.en: Do you know about the new overtime rule?
example.zh: 你知道新的加班规定吗？

entries.l1_note: know about 是了解；know of 是听说过。

entries.head: make of

senses.en: to have an opinion about something

example.en: What do you make of his sudden resignation?
example.zh: 他突然辞职，你怎么看？

entries.l1_note: What do you make of...? 是“你怎么看”，不是“你做了什么”。
collocations: what do you make of it

entries.head: see as

senses.en: to think of someone or something in a particular way

example.en: The team sees the delay as a chance to fix the design.
example.zh: 团队把延期看成修正设计的机会。

entries.l1_note: see A as B；as 不能换成 like。

entries.head: begin with

senses.en: to start with something

example.en: The meeting will begin with a short update.
example.zh: 会议先做一个简短通报。

entries.l1_note: begin with + 内容；begin by doing 是“先做某事”。

entries.head: do with

senses.en: to be connected with something

example.en: I have nothing to do with the scheduling change.
example.zh: 排期变动跟我没关系。

entries.l1_note: have to do with 是“与…有关”；do with 还可表示“需要/处理”。
collocations: have to do with a decision

entries.head: go off on

senses.en: to start talking about something unrelated

example.en: He went off on a tangent about his old job.
example.zh: 他跑题讲起了以前的工作。

entries.l1_note: go off on a tangent 是固定说法；不是“离开去某地”。

entries.head: get straight to the point

senses.en: to say the most important thing without delay

example.en: Let's get straight to the point — we need a decision today.
example.zh: 直说吧，我们今天需要拍板。

entries.l1_note: get straight to the point / get to the point；不要绕圈子。

entries.head: change the subject

senses.en: to start talking about something else

example.en: Every time I mention rent, he changes the subject.
example.zh: 每次我一提房租，他就换话题。

entries.l1_note: change the subject 是换话题；不是“改科目”。

entries.head: keep someone posted

senses.en: to keep giving someone the latest information

example.en: Keep me posted about the interview result.
example.zh: 面试结果随时告诉我。

entries.l1_note: keep someone posted 是“随时告知”；posted 不是“邮寄”。

entries.head: hit it off with

senses.en: to like each other immediately

example.en: She hit it off with her new roommates right away.
example.zh: 她跟新室友一见如故。

entries.l1_note: hit it off with someone；不是“打它”。

entries.head: get wires crossed

senses.en: to misunderstand each other

example.en: We got our wires crossed about the meeting time.
example.zh: 我们把开会时间搞错了。

entries.l1_note: get one's wires crossed 是“沟通误会”；别直译成“电线交叉”。

entries.head: be in touch with

senses.en: to keep communicating with someone

example.en: Are you still in touch with your old coworkers?
example.zh: 你还跟老同事有联系吗？

entries.l1_note: be in touch with = 保持联系；get in touch with = 联系上。

entries.head: get in touch with

senses.en: to contact someone

example.en: I'll get in touch with the client this afternoon.
example.zh: 我下午联系客户。

entries.l1_note: get in touch with someone = 联系上；be in touch with = 保持联系。
collocations: get in touch with a client

entries.head: keep in touch with

senses.en: to continue communicating with someone

example.en: We keep in touch with our old neighbors on WeChat.
example.zh: 我们跟老邻居在微信上保持联系。

entries.l1_note: keep in touch with someone；也可以说 stay in touch。

entries.head: lose touch with

senses.en: to stop communicating with someone

example.en: I lost touch with my college friends after moving.
example.zh: 搬家后我跟大学朋友失去了联系。

entries.l1_note: lose touch with someone；反义是 keep in touch with。

entries.head: not breathe a word

senses.en: to not tell anyone a secret

example.en: Don't breathe a word about the surprise party.
example.zh: 惊喜派对的事一个字都别说。

entries.l1_note: not breathe a word about something；不是“不呼吸”。
collocations: not breathe a word about it

entries.head: keep quiet

senses.en: to not tell anyone about something

example.en: Keep quiet about the raise until it's official.
example.zh: 加薪的事官宣前先别说。

entries.l1_note: keep quiet about something 是保密；keep quiet 也可表示保持安静。

entries.head: zip it

senses.en: to stop talking, used rudely

example.en: Zip it — the manager is coming.
example.zh: 别说了，经理来了。

entries.l1_note: zip it 是口语“闭嘴”，不礼貌；正式场合别用。

entries.head: go back to

senses.en: 回到（话题）

example.en: Let's go back to the first slide for a minute.
example.zh: 我们回到第一页幻灯片看一下。

entries.l1_note: go back to + 话题；不是“走回去”。

entries.head: drop someone a line

senses.en: 给某人发个消息

example.en: Drop me a line when you land.
example.zh: 落地后给我发个消息。

entries.l1_note: drop someone a line 是发消息/写信；不是“扔线”。

entries.head: get a hold of

senses.en: 联系上

example.en: I couldn't get a hold of the driver.
example.zh: 我没联系上司机。

entries.l1_note: get a hold of someone 是联系上；不是“抓住”。

entries.head: go to someone

senses.en: 找某人帮忙

example.en: Go to her if you need help with the forms.
example.zh: 填表有困难就找她。

entries.l1_note: go to someone 是找某人帮忙；不是“去某人那里”。
